edges.description: Merlin restrains the Hippo effectors; losing it releases them. How it does so is contested, and the entry carries that as a discussion rather than choosing: one body of work has merlin recruiting LATS to the plasma membrane, another has it acting in the nucleus on a ubiquitin ligase that inhibits LATS there.
The tumour. The cell type is Schwann, and why this lineage rather than another is the question the cited review says is unanswered.
The tumour as the finding that defines the disease.
A benign tumour in a bony canal. What it does is mechanical, and it is the route to every auditory and vestibular phenotype in this entry.

nodes.description: An anti-VEGF antibody, and the only drug in this entry with a pooled response rate. Across 161 patients and 196 assessable tumours, 41% had partial regression and 47% no change; hearing improved in 20% and was stable in 69%. Seventeen per cent had serious toxicity.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of bevacizumab for vestibular schwannoma in neurofibromatosis type 2: a systematic review and meta-analysis of treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: In patients with assessable audiometric data, bevacizumab treatment resulted in hearing improvement in 20% (95% CI 9-33%), stability in 69% (95% CI 51-85%) and additional loss in 6% (95% CI 1-15%) Serious bevacizumab toxicity was observed in 17% (95% CI 10-26%).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of bevacizumab for vestibular schwannoma in neurofibromatosis type 2: a systematic review and meta-analysis of treatment outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Bevacizumab may arrest both tumor progression and hearing loss in select NF2 patients presenting with VS lesions. However, a considerable proportion of patients are anticipated to experience serious adverse events; correspondingly, judicious use of bevacizumab for symptomatic management of VS in NF2 is recommended.

evidence.reference_title: Synergistic effect of PAK and Hippo pathway inhibitor combination in NF2-deficient Schwannoma.
evidence.snippet: The most successful therapy to date has been the anti-VEGF drug bevacizumab. However, there are long term concerns for patients who start bevacizumab during adolescence, so many pediatric NF2 patients, who often have the most severe form of the disease, are restricted to surgical treatment.

evidence.reference_title: History and clinical epidemiology of NF2-related schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: However, none have been approved by regulatory bodies for the treatment of NF2 driven tumors and are therefore used off label but with endorsement of national health agencies [ 64 , 66 ].

nodes.description: The hallmark, in 95% of patients and on its own sufficient for the diagnosis. HPO has a term for the bilateral form specifically, a child of HP:0009588 Vestibular schwannoma, and the row binds that rather than the laterality-neutral parent.

evidence.reference_title: Neurofibromatosis Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Vestibular schwannomas are the hallmark lesion, affecting 95% of individuals and typically occur bilaterally.

evidence.snippet: Almost all affected individuals develop bilateral vestibular schwannomas by age 30 years.

nodes.description: In about 70% of patients, though only 10% have ten or more, and much subtler than the skin findings of neurofibromatosis type 1. It can be the presenting feature in childhood.

evidence.reference_title: History and clinical epidemiology of NF2-related schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: About 70% of NF2-SWN patients have cutaneous schwannomas, but only 10% have 10 or more [ 9 ].

nodes.description: One inactivated NF2 allele in every cell. On its own it produces no tumour; it sets the threshold at a single further event.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular biology of NF2/Merlin on tumorigenesis and development.
evidence.snippet: The neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) gene, known for encoding the tumor suppressor protein Merlin, is central to the study of tumorigenesis and associated cellular processes.

nodes.description: Merlin sits at the membrane and restrains proliferation through several pathways at once - Hippo, Wnt, mTOR, receptor tyrosine kinase signalling and others. The cited review lists them; it does not rank them or say which carries the tumour in which cell type, and this entry does not either.

biological_processes: negative regulation of cell population proliferation

evidence.reference_title: The molecular biology of NF2/Merlin on tumorigenesis and development.
evidence.snippet: This review comprehensively examines the multifaceted role of NF2/Merlin, detailing its structural characteristics, functional diversity, and involvement in various signaling pathways such as Wnt/beta-catenin, Hippo, TGF-beta, RTKs, mTOR, Notch, and Hedgehog.

nodes.description: The second commonest tumour, with a lifetime risk approaching 80%, and sometimes the presenting one, particularly in children.

evidence.reference_title: Classification of schwannomas and the new naming convention for "neurofibromatosis-2": Genetic updates and international consensus recommendation.
evidence.snippet: Notably, NF2 patients characteristically present with bilateral vestibular schwannomas (VS). Additionally, they have a high lifetime risk of developing meningiomas (approaching 80%), and a significant proportion (20-30%) may also develop spinal cord ependymomas.

evidence.reference_title: Classification of schwannomas and the new naming convention for "neurofibromatosis-2": Genetic updates and international consensus recommendation.
evidence.snippet: Meningiomas represent the second most prevalent tumor type observed in NF2-related SWN, surpassing sporadic meningiomas in terms of earlier onset. Notably, meningiomas can even be the presenting feature, particularly in pediatric patients.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular biology of NF2/Merlin on tumorigenesis and development.
evidence.snippet: Neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) is an inherited genetic disorder that follows an autosomal dominant pattern, affecting around 1 in 40 000 individuals, 1 and results from the inactivation of the neurofibromin 2 (NF2) gene that is located in the long arm of chromosome 22 (22q), and this gene encodes a protein called Merlin

evidence.reference_title: The molecular biology of NF2/Merlin on tumorigenesis and development.
evidence.snippet: NF2 mutations are specifically linked to the development of schwannomas, meningiomas, and ependymomas, although the precise mechanisms of tumor formation in these specific cell types remain unclear.

nodes.description: Schwann-cell tumours, of which the vestibular ones define the disease. Meningiomas and ependymomas arise by the same two-hit route in arachnoid and ependymal cells and are recorded as phenotypes rather than as separate nodes, because no cited source gives them a different mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Vestibular Schwannoma: What We Know and Where We are Heading.
evidence.snippet: Vestibular schwannoma (VS) is a Schwann cell-derived tumour arising from the vestibulocochlear nerve.

evidence.reference_title: Neurofibromatosis Type 2.
evidence.snippet: Vestibular schwannomas are the hallmark lesion, affecting 95% of individuals and typically occur bilaterally.

nodes.description: The deficit that carries most of the disease's burden, and one that progresses in the untreated: about 4 dB a year in a cohort followed nine years. The row carries no frequency band for the same reason the tinnitus row does not: the cited sources name hearing loss among the characteristic symptoms without giving a proportion of patients, and the one figure available - over 60% - comes from a review of vestibular schwannoma generally rather than of this syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Natural history of hearing and tumor growth in vestibular schwannoma in neurofibromatosis type 2-related schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: The average follow-up period was approximately 9 years, and hearing deteriorated at an average rate of approximately 4 dB/year.

evidence.reference_title: NF2-Related Schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: NF2-related schwannomatosis (NF2) is characterized by bilateral vestibular schwannomas with associated symptoms of tinnitus, hearing loss, and balance dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Natural history of hearing and tumor growth in vestibular schwannoma in neurofibromatosis type 2-related schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: Although the hearing preservation rate in NF2 cases is poor with the current treatment methods, many cases exist in which hearing acuity deteriorates, even during the natural course.

nodes.description: Biallelic inactivation in a single cell, which is where a tumour begins. The cell types that tolerate it and grow are Schwann cells, arachnoid cells and ependymal cells; why those and not others is not established by any cited source.

nodes.description: In 20 to 30% of patients, typically multiple, intramedullary, slow-growing and asymptomatic. HPO has a term for the histology but none for the spinal or intramedullary site, so the binding gives the tumour type and the preferred term carries where it sits. The row is the reason gliomas were dropped from the diagnostic criteria and ependymoma added.

evidence.reference_title: Classification of schwannomas and the new naming convention for "neurofibromatosis-2": Genetic updates and international consensus recommendation.
evidence.snippet: Spinal ependymomas, the most commonly diagnosed gliomas in NF2-related SWN, may occur as multiple intramedullary, slow-growing, asymptomatic masses 1 (Figure 2).

evidence.reference_title: History and clinical epidemiology of NF2-related schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: The predominance of intrasmedullary tumours being spinal ependymomas and absence of high-grade gliomas has now been confirmed

nodes.description: A single dose to the tumour, less applicable to large lesions. Hearing preservation falls with time rather than holding: from about half at five years to a third at ten and fifteen. GeneReviews lists radiation of NF2-associated tumours among the agents and circumstances to avoid, especially in childhood, where it judges the malignancy risk likely to be substantially higher - so this row is not a first option in a child.

evidence.reference_title: Vestibular Schwannoma: What We Know and Where We are Heading.
evidence.snippet: A more recent case-controlled study found that hearing preservation amongst patients decreases from 53% at 5 years to 34% at 10 and 15 years amongst all tumour grades [ 64 ].

evidence.reference_title: Neurofibromatosis type 2 and related disorders.
evidence.snippet: Cohort studies found survival analysis to hearing loss and unilateral visual loss in severe mutation groups was 32 and 38 years; active management gave better outcomes than surveillance in spinal ependymoma; gamma knife, bevacizumab and hearing preservation surgery maintained or improved short-term hearing in selected patients, and gamma knife had a good long-term tumour control in mild patients with small tumours.

evidence.reference_title: NF2-Related Schwannomatosis.
evidence.snippet: Radiation therapy of NF2-associated tumors, especially in childhood, when malignancy risks are likely to be substantially higher.

nodes.description: Translabyrinthine and retrosigmoid approaches are the usual ones. The first sacrifices hearing and is used where there is little to lose; the second preserves it better at a higher risk to the facial and cochlear nerves. In this syndrome the tumours are larger and multiple, and one review attributes lower surgical efficacy and higher complication rates to that.

evidence.reference_title: Vestibular Schwannoma: What We Know and Where We are Heading.
evidence.snippet: A major disadvantage is poor preservation of hearing, limiting the use of the TL approach to those with minimal or absent preoperative hearing.

evidence.snippet: led to the designation of four treatment centres to manage all NF2-SWN patients in England commissioned in 2009 resulting in further improvement in survival

evidence.snippet: The most frequent clinical manifestations include hearing loss, tinnitus, and balance dysfunction, likely secondary to the bilateral VS which is a characteristic of this mixed neuro-cutaneous disorder.

nodes.description: Progressive compression of the cochlear and vestibular nerves, and at larger volumes of the brainstem. Hearing falls as the tumour grows: in an untreated cohort followed about nine years, hearing deteriorated by roughly 4 dB a year and tumour volume and hearing loss were correlated.

nodes.description: Unphosphorylated YAP and TAZ enter the nucleus and drive TEAD-dependent transcription. In a mouse already carrying a Lats1/2 lesion, gene dosage sets how much tumour the animal gets and how long it lives, and one surviving YAP or TAZ allele is enough for a schwannoma to form. That is a statement about how much YAP and TAZ activity the tumour needs, not about a YAP allele initiating one on its own.

biological_processes: TEAD-dependent transcriptional activation by YAP and TAZ

evidence.reference_title: Schwannoma development is mediated by Hippo pathway dysregulation and modified by RAS/MAPK signaling.
evidence.snippet: These data suggest that YAP/TAZ gene dosage determines tumor burden and survival, and that a single allele of YAP or TAZ is sufficient for schwannoma formation.

evidence.reference_title: Merlin/NF2 loss-driven tumorigenesis linked to CRL4(DCAF1)-mediated inhibition of the hippo pathway kinases Lats1 and 2 in the nucleus.
evidence.snippet: There was a strong positive correlation of nuclear YAP staining and weak or absent cytoplasmic P-YAP staining in tumors with low Merlin expression (p=0.001 for YAP and p=0.001 for phospho-YAP, Mann-Whitney U test), indicating that loss of Merlin causes activation of YAP via reduced phosphorylation and increased accumulation in the nucleus.
